_comment: Benchmarks the nightly job must report (T-1801), checked by tools/benchmark/compare_benchmarks.py --required. Keys are className.testName; each listed metric prefix must match at least one reported metric. A benchmark that is intentionally not run by the job goes under optional with its reason. A result that is neither required nor optional fails the gate, so a renamed test cannot slip through. The listed metrics are the ones a GitHub-hosted emulator reports: it has no SurfaceFlinger frame timeline, so FrameTimingMetric yields frameCount alone and the jank metrics frameDurationCpuMs and frameOverrunMs of plan §9 need a physical device (ADR-0018 addendum).

optional.ir.taqvim.benchmark.BaselineProfileGener: Excluded from the nightly job (notClass); run on demand by :app:generateBaselineProfile.

optional.ir.taqvim.benchmark.micro.GlanceWidgetBe: Run, but not required: T-1216 is new and has no committed baseline. Like every case in this class it times GlanceAppWidget.compose end to end, which is dominated by Glance's fixed per-call cost, so it is not a render time and plan §9's 30 ms does not apply to it.

The paired experiment of L4, and not a budgeted figure. An empty widget and a populated one are composed alternately, swapping which goes first, so both sides share their conditions; `timeNs` is the per-pair signed difference and `emptyNs`/`populatedNs` are the sides it came from. Its spread, not its median, is what is being looked at: tight means Glance's fixed per-call cost is additive and subtracting it leaves a real quantity, wide means the subtraction is noise. Until that has been read off a device run, such a difference is an incremental wall-clock estimate and is not called a composition cost.

control._comment: Runner-health control (T-1801). These microbenchmarks time fixed synthetic drawing and mask computation in process, with no UI, no frame timeline and no dataset, so a change to the app's screens or data cannot move them. When they move far, the machine moved: both degraded nightly runs blew them up while the code that draws them was byte-identical to the baseline commit (run 35953669737 sunArcBitmap +348.8 %, progressRingBitmap +241.3 %; run 36040359691 progressRingBitmap +258.4 %, moonBitmap +75.6 %). A control outside its band makes the whole comparison inconclusive rather than failed, because timings from that machine cannot be trusted. Editing the code one of these benchmarks draws means its baseline must be re-recorded, as for any benchmark. GlanceWidgetBenchmark's cases are deliberately not here and deliberately not budgeted: they time GlanceAppWidget.compose end to end, which is dominated by a fixed per-call cost of roughly 405 ms that moves neither with widget content nor with the speed of the machine. Plan §9's 30 ms render budget belongs to WidgetRenderBenchmark, which times the painters with no Glance harness around them.
